title: Enforcing Trust Accountability with Backward Propagation

problem.claim: Reliable interactions in distributed networks require trust and reputation management, including accountability for propagated trust signals and initialization of newly joined nodes.

gap.claim: Existing trust models rely on forward propagation, lack robust accountability mechanisms for negative interactions, and often fail to initialize nodes with sparse interaction histories.

contributions.claim: RepuLink is a two-layer reputation model coupling an endorsement network with an interaction feedback network.

RepuLink introduces backward endorsement penalty propagation for recursively penalizing endorsers of misbehaving nodes and backward endorsement reward propagation for rewarding endorsers of well-performing nodes.
The endorsement layer provides explainable, endorser-weighted trust initialization for newly joined nodes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets against representative trust propagation baselines report that RepuLink outperforms across four evaluation metrics in interaction-only and full two-layer settings.
The experiments report comparable efficiency to the representative trust propagation baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Trust and reputation management supports reliable interactions in distributed networks.
Forward-only trust models lack accountability for negative interactions and struggle with cold-start initialization.
RepuLink couples endorsement and interaction feedback networks and applies backward penalty and reward propagation.
The coupled design aims to enforce endorsement accountability, incentivize positive behavior, and provide explainable trust initialization.
Experiments report improvements across four metrics with comparable efficiency in two evaluation settings.

source_observation.claim: Backward propagation penalizes endorsers of misbehaving nodes and rewards endorsers of well-performing nodes.

interpretation.claim: Propagating accountability through endorsement relationships can align endorsement incentives with downstream behavior.

application.claim: In systems where agents endorse or delegate trust, consider feedback mechanisms that assign consequences or rewards to endorsers based on endorsed-agent outcomes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether backward propagation is appropriate when endorsement relationships are unreliable, strategic, or difficult to attribute.

source_observation.claim: The endorsement layer provides explainable, endorser-weighted trust initialization for newly joined nodes.

interpretation.claim: A separate endorsement structure can provide interpretable priors for entities with sparse direct interaction history.

application.claim: For cold-start settings, use attributable endorsements as an initialization signal alongside direct interaction evidence.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how endorsement quality, bias, or manipulation risk is controlled.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the real-world datasets or representative baselines.
The four evaluation metrics and their numerical results are unspecified.
The abstract does not describe experimental protocols, statistical uncertainty, or efficiency measurements.
The abstract does not specify the propagation algorithms' convergence, parameterization, or failure conditions.
